records.reason: The authors state that this study retests the perceptual body-image differences in the cited original, using a revised design. The reference list identifies this candidate as reference 17. The only supplied shipped row is Cornelissen et al. (2016), “Visual biases in judging body weight,” a distinct article (reference 20), so it does not represent this original work.
records.location: Introduction (replication aim); References 17/18; supplied shipped row 1858
records.omission_quote: In summary, the current study serves both as a replication and extension of Cornelissen et al. [17,18]. We aimed to replicate the differences in perceptual body image identified in these previous studies by improving the design in the following ways: a) ensuring a more accurate alignment of actual BMI ranges across participant groups, b) incorporating measures to control for sociocultural attitudes towards appearance, and c) implementing a refined psychophysical method for body size estimation that avoided emotionally loaded language in the responses.
